aggregate_terms.definition: A flexible strategy built on efficient threats, answers, and repeatable value.
Creating token permanents, especially creature tokens, as resources or threats.
A reactive strategy that answers threats and wins after stabilizing.
A proactive strategy that pressures opponents early through damage or threats.
Using the graveyard as an active game zone or resource.
Getting access to more mana than normal for your turn count.
Sacrificing your own permanents for value, protection, or triggers.
Protection from a quality prevents damage, enchanting or equipping, blocking, and targeting from sources with that quality; it does not stop effects that do none of those things.
Rewarding the casting of instants and sorceries, often in chains.
Winning through creatures dying, sacrifice loops, and drain or value payoffs.
Using counters on permanents or players as a scaling resource.
Gaining advantage by making opponents spend more time and mana than you do.
Producing very large amounts of mana for oversized plays.
Reset many permanents at once when one-for-one interaction is not enough.
Using Equipment artifacts to enhance creatures repeatedly.
Leave lands or other mana sources untapped so you can act later.
Casting many spells in one turn, sometimes using the Storm keyword.
Make selected actions cost more mana or other resources.
Develop mostly on other players' turns; in Commander, keep mana open for draw, counters, or instant-speed interaction.
Constrain which actions remain available by using rule-setting permanents and taxes to narrow opposing lines.
Putting cards from your own library into your graveyard on purpose.
A creature with trample can assign excess combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle it is attacking after assigning lethal damage to its blockers.
Building one creature, often a commander, into a lethal protected threat.
A spellslinger plan that builds mana and spell count toward a concentrated turn of large spells; it may use the Storm keyword, but does not have to.
Exiling permanents and returning them to reuse enter-the-battlefield effects or dodge removal.
Colorless mana is mana with no color. A {C} cost can be paid only with colorless mana.
As you cast a spell with convoke, your creatures can be tapped to help pay its mana cost; each tapped creature pays for one mana of its color or one generic mana.
Temporarily stop a permanent from attacking, blocking, or activating non-mana abilities.
A card with devoid is colorless even if colored mana symbols appear in its mana cost. Devoid does not remove those colors from the card's Commander color identity.
Devour lets a creature enter with +1/+1 counters for each creature sacrificed as it enters; Devour N gives N counters per creature.
Using effects that trigger when permanents enter the battlefield.
A generic mana cost is shown with a number and can be paid with mana of any color or with colorless mana; it is a cost, not a type of mana.
Until your next turn, a goaded creature attacks each combat if able and attacks a player other than you if able.
Triggering effects when lands enter the battlefield under your control.
Getting access to more mana than normal for your turn count.
Create a token that's a copy of a creature token you control.
Copying instants, sorceries, or other spells for extra effects.
Wastes is a basic land with no land types that taps for one colorless mana; a Commander deck may include any number of it.
Small creatures that restrict opponents' actions while applying pressure.
A board or resource state that appears even; breaking parity means benefiting more than opponents from a symmetrical rule or reset.
Make attacking you less attractive or more expensive without necessarily stopping the whole table.
Restricting resources, actions, or timing so opponents cannot execute normal plans.

terms.definition: Producing very large amounts of mana for oversized plays.
Colorless mana is mana with no color. A {C} cost can be paid only with colorless mana.
A card with devoid is colorless even if colored mana symbols appear in its mana cost. Devoid does not remove those colors from the card's Commander color identity.
A generic mana cost is shown with a number and can be paid with mana of any color or with colorless mana; it is a cost, not a type of mana.
